newsitem.title: USA: Faulding says no papers yet for suit.
newsitem.headline: Faulding says no papers yet for suit.

text.p: Australian pharmaceuticals group F.H. Faulding has not yet been served with legal papers in a suit over a morphine analgesic launched by the company internationally this year, chief executive Ed Tweddell said. U.S. based Faulding Inc, 73 percent owned by F.H. Faulding, secured U.S. Federal Drug Administration approval this year for Kadian, an oral sustained release morphine product.

The drug, distributed nationally in the United States for about a month by Zeneca Inc, aims to tap the $US500 million cancer-pain control market and more specifically the $185 million controlled release segment of the market, dominated
until recently by a product from Purdue Frederick Co.

Purdue Frederick filed a lawsuit in August alleging that the manufacture and marketing of Kadian in the United States infringed a U.S. patent assigned to it and constituted an unfair competitive practice under federal and state law.
"We believe the case is without merit," Tweddell said on Wednesday.
"It did not interfere with the launch of the product and both Zeneca and Faulding will work together, if infact it is served on us, to defend the Kadian patent," Tweddell said.
Tweddell, speaking at the McIntosh Securities Investment Conference in New York, said sales of Kadian in the United States were meeting expectations.
